titleTr: Dersin değerlendirmesi: needn't have ve should have

grammar.topic: needn't have / should have / shouldn't have + V3
explainTr: Should have + V3, geçmişte yapılmayan ama yapılması gereken şeyi anlatır: I should have checked the handout. (Kontrol etmedim, etmeliydim.) Shouldn't have + V3, yapılmaması gerekirdi anlamına gelir: I shouldn't have shouted.
Needn't have + V3, bir şeyi yaptığını ama gerek olmadığını söyler: I needn't have made so many posters. (Yaptım, ama gerek yoktu.)
Dikkat: didn't need to ise gereksizdi demek, ama yapıp yapmadığın belli olmaz. Needn't have'de iş yapılmıştır.
grammar.compareTr: Türkçede 'yapmalıydım' ve 'yapmama gerek yoktu' ayrı kelimelerle söylenir. İngilizcede her ikisi de 'have + V3' ile kurulur: should have done / needn't have done.

examples.en: You should have called me earlier.
We shouldn't have left the door open.
I needn't have brought an umbrella; it didn't rain.
examples.tr: Şemsiye getirmeme gerek yoktu; yağmur yağmadı.

reading.title: Hafsa evaluates her lesson
reading.text:
On Friday afternoon, Hafsa sat in Ms. Carter's classroom after school. She had taught her first full lesson that day, and now she wanted to evaluate it honestly. Ms. Carter had given her a simple form with three questions: What went well? What didn't? What would you change?

Hafsa started with the good news. The objective of the lesson was to practice new vocabulary through a short story. The students listened carefully, and many of them participated in the discussion. A shy girl, Sofia, even raised her hand twice. Hafsa had praised her, and Sofia smiled all afternoon.

Then she moved to the difficult part. "I should have checked the instructions before class," she wrote. "My handout was confusing, and several students did not know what to do." Because of that, she had to explain the task three times. She had also talked too quickly. "I should have used a slower pace. Some students struggled to follow."

There was one more thing. Hafsa had spent two hours the night before making colorful posters for the board. During the lesson, she hardly used them. "I needn't have made so many posters," she wrote. "They were nice, but unnecessary, and they distracted some children." She laughed at herself and added a small smiling face.

When Ms. Carter read the form, she nodded. "This is a very honest evaluation," she said. "Many new teachers only see the mistakes. You also saw what worked. And you are right about the handout. You could have shown the students an example first."

"I know," said Hafsa. "Next time I'll give an example, I'll speak more slowly, and I'll use fewer materials."

"That's exactly the kind of feedback that helps a lesson improve," Ms. Carter said. "A good teacher doesn't have to be perfect. She just has to keep learning."

On the way home, Hafsa felt tired but happy. She was already thinking about her next lesson, and she had one more idea: a short quiz game at the end of the class.

questions.q: What does Ms. Carter say about a good teacher?
questions.whyTr: Ms. Carter: She just has to keep learning.

script.speaker: Ms. Carter
script.text: Hafsa, how do you feel about your lesson today?

script.speaker: Hafsa
script.text: Mixed. The students enjoyed the story, but the handout was confusing. I should have tested it first.

script.speaker: Ms. Carter
script.text: Good point. What else would you change?

script.speaker: Hafsa
script.text: I spoke too fast. I should have slowed down, especially for the students who struggle with English.

script.speaker: Ms. Carter
script.text: I agree. But I also noticed that you gave a lot of praise. That was effective.

script.speaker: Hafsa
script.text: Thank you. Sofia participated for the first time, so I was very happy.

script.speaker: Ms. Carter
script.text: What about the materials? You brought so many posters.

script.speaker: Hafsa
script.text: I needn't have made them. I stayed up until midnight, and the children hardly looked at them.

script.speaker: Ms. Carter
script.text: Next time, keep it simple. One clear objective, one good activity.

script.speaker: Hafsa
script.text: That makes sense. Should I write a short evaluation for the principal?

script.speaker: Ms. Carter
script.text: Yes. Mention the outcome, the problems, and your plan to improve.

script.speaker: Hafsa
script.text: I'll write it tonight. Thank you for your feedback.

writing.promptTr: Bir dersi veya etkinliği değerlendiren kısa bir yazı yaz. Ne yapmalıydın (should have), neyi yapmamalıydın (shouldn't have) ve neye gerek yoktu (needn't have) anlat. 120-180 kelime.
writing.promptEn: Write a short evaluation of a lesson or an event. Use should have, shouldn't have and needn't have to describe what you would change (120-180 words).
writing.model: Overall, my lesson on Friday went fairly well. The objective was to practice new vocabulary through a short story, and most students participated. I praised a shy girl, Sofia, and she was very happy. However, I should have checked the instructions before class. The handout was confusing, so I had to explain the activity three times. I also should have spoken more slowly because some students struggled to follow me. I shouldn't have given so many tasks in one lesson, because the children became tired. In addition, I needn't have made so many colorful posters. I spent two hours on them, but the students hardly looked at them, and they distracted a few children. Next time, I will give an example first, use a slower pace, and prepare fewer materials. I think these changes will improve the outcome. I am grateful for Ms. Carter's feedback, and I am excited about my next lesson.

Hem iyi hem zayıf yönleri yazdın mı?
Yapıdan sonra fiili V3 yaptın mı?
Gelecek için bir plan cümlen var mı?
